iconicAnchor.label: Museum and culture magazine feature spreads
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Magazine editors, art directors, photographers, and writers
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The Met's discussion of Hanatsubaki documents a sustained magazine identity in which photography, illustration, fashion, typography, and changing editorial direction combine across issues and spreads.

sources.title: Library: Hanatsubaki Magazine
supports: The publication history shows magazine art direction as an evolving relationship among imagery, typography, culture, and editorial purpose.
The reproduced issues and spreads support strong openers within a continuous publication identity.

sources.title: Design Journal, Spring/Summer 2017
supports: The journal provides complete institutional feature layouts combining headlines, essays, photographs, captions, and page-to-page pacing.
Its spread sequence demonstrates that a feature system must work after the opener, not only on one dramatic page.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches feature opener, headline deck, pull quote, image text pacing, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/magazine-feature/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
